independentFocusedRun.runtime: Windows x64, Node v24.16.0, ABI 137, reused source-only snapshot

verification.semanticRedEvidence: The S10 evidence records exit-1 assertion failures before the corresponding behavior changes for equal-time latest acceptance, durable enumeration, restart convergence, failed-job retry, dead and partial lock recovery, stale replay, concurrent publisher wait, repeated-content publication, and transient startup acceptance retry. Setup or native ABI failures were not counted as RED.
verification.redChronologyLimit: Original preimplementation RED transcripts and source snapshots were not retained. The assertion names and chronology are author-reported and cannot be independently reconstructed from the final tree.

assessment: The final S10 case uses real temporary filesystem and SQLite state, plus a separate publisher process. Existing S08 and S09 assertions were adapted for publication-order identities without removing their safety expectations.

A durable private publication order selects the actual latest new-schema intent across equal millisecond timestamps, clock rollback, concurrent publication and concurrent owner acceptance. An atomic, flushed lock owner file avoids half-written owner records; a stale partial legacy directory is recovered after an age guard. A live owner is not stolen.

The owner resumes private intents on startup one per event-loop turn and retries transient failures with bounded backoff. The test observes automatic recovery after a real SQLite trigger abort without a caller re-save.

The ledger persists desired revisions and hashes, keeps a save during active indexing dirty, rejects a second active claim, creates a fresh retry job after terminal failure, and traverses more than one keyset page without omissions or duplicates. The public MCP schema is unchanged; S11 completion races and S12 keyword cache writes are not claimed complete.
documentedLimits: A witness-free legacy pair with the same body and timestamp cannot reveal its true publication order; it remains fail-closed with file and provenance preserved.
A dead lock owner's PID reused by another process cannot be distinguished portably with the Node process probe; recovery fails closed and requires later inspection or recovery work.
